contexts.text: The Lord blessing and saying (), that is, operating.
Jehovah said unto Cain () = that conscience dictated. ( = something perceptive within which dictated concerning charity. AC 370.)
Cain said unto Abel () = a space of time.
Cain said unto Jehovah () = a certain confession...
God said () = that so it was. AC 1037. AC 1315.
Jehovah said unto Noah () = that it was so done.

Jehovah said in His heart () = that it would not any more be so done. For, when it is predicated of Jehovah that He says, it means that it is so, or is not so; for of Jehovah nothing else can be said than that He is.
God said... () = the Truth of the things which follow... AC 1020.
They said a man to his companion () = that it was begun...
They said () = that it was so done.
Sayings, occurs. AC 1406.
Jehovah said unto Abram () = the first mental advertence.

In the Ancient Church, when anything was true, they said Jehovah said, or Jehovah spake, which signified that so it was. But, after significatives had been turned into representatives, the Lord did actually speak with them, and when it is said then that Jehovah said, or spoke, to anyone, it = the same as before; and therefore (the above words) = the first mental advertence; just as when, in the Ancient Church, anyone adverted by conscience, by some other dictate, or by their Word, that it was so, it was said, in like manner, that Jehovah said.
Abram said, Lord Jehovih () = the Lord's perception. Explained. So wherever this expression is used.
He believes it simply, because the Lord has said so; and he who so believes does no evil, although it should not be true in itself... AC 1911:6.
The perception which the Lord had was... from Jehovah Himself, which is here signified by Jehovah said unto him. AC 1822. AC 1841.
Sarai said unto Abram () = that (the affection of truth) so perceived. AC 1913.
Abram said unto Sarai () = a perception... The Lord's perception was represented by Abram said to Sarai; but thought from perception by Sarai said to Abram.
God said unto Abraham () = a perception. AC 2061.
Abraham said unto God () = the Lord's perception from love. To say to God = to perceive.
The thought and speech of the Spiritual Angels are determined to the subject according to the series of the sayings.
Jehovah said unto Abraham () = the Lord's perception from the Divine. AC 2224.
When Jehovah said occurs, it = a perception which is not altogether continuous with the former one; but a sequent one, and sometimes a new one. AC 2260.
He said () = exhortation.
The men said unto Lot () = that the Lord draws the attention of those in the good of charity.
Abraham said () = thought.
God said unto Abimelech () = a thought from perception. Explained.
To say = to think. AC 2560.
Doctrine is to be believed because the Lord has said so. (See Affirmative.)
Abimelech said () = the Lord's perception; (for) to say = to think...
To Sarah he said () = a perception from spiritual truth.
The perception which is signified by Jehovah said () was from the Divine Celestial; but the thought which is signified by Jehovah spake, was from the Divine Celestial through the Divine Spiritual...

Good is of love... and therefore perception is from it; but truth is of faith, and consequently this is of thought: the former is signified... by to say, and the latter by to speak. But when to say occurs alone, it sometimes = to perceive, and sometimes to think; because to say involves both.
Sarah said () = a perception from the Divine Spiritual.
And she said () = thought. To say = to perceive, and also to think.
Abraham said () = a perception from the Divine.
God said unto Abraham () = the Lord's perception from the Divine. AC 2769.
The Angel of God... said to her, What aileth thee, Hagar? () = perception concerning its state. (Explained.)
God said = to perceive from Divine truth. AC 2810.
He said, occurs four times in this verse (); (for) it is usual in the Word, when any new thing is begun, to say and he said.
To speak, and say = to think and perceive.
The servant said unto him () = the Lord's perception concerning the natural man.
Abraham said unto him () = the Lord's perception from the Divine.
(The servant) said () = a communication. To say = to perceive and will; and (therefore) to communicate; for communication is from perceiving and willing.
To say = to perceive, thus also to explore. AC 3204.
Jehovah said = to perceive from the Divine.
Esau said to Jacob () = the Lord's perception from the good of the Natural.
Jehovah appeared to him, and said () = thought from the Divine.
Abimelech called Isaac and said () = the Lord's perception from doctrine. AC 3414.
That to say = to perceive and think, is more manifestly evident here AC 3554 than elsewhere.
Jehovah appeared to him in that night, and said () = the Lord's perception concerning that obscurity.
Rebekah said unto Jacob her son () = the Lord's perception from Divine truth concerning natural truth.
Jacob said unto Rebekah his mother () = the Lord's perception from Divine truth concerning natural truth. AC 3531.
Jacob said unto his father () = the apperception of natural truth. To say = to perceive; here, to apperceive, because from the Natural.
Isaac said unto his son () = the perception of the Rational concerning the Natural. AC 3558.
The reason it is so often said he said, is that thus what is new begins, or a new perception.
Isaac his father answered and said unto (Esau) () = a perception concerning natural good, that it would become Divine.
Esau said in his heart () = thought.
To call to him, and say to him () = a state of perception.
Laban said unto him () = a perception from that good (Laban).
Jehovah said unto Jacob () = the Lord's perception from the Divine.
The Angel of God said unto me () = a perception from the Divine.
Laban said unto Jacob () = a state of communication (between these two goods).
Laban answered and said unto Jacob () = an obscure state of perception.
Shechem said unto Hamor... () = a thought from the truth which was among the Ancients. To say = perception and thence thought.
To say, here () = to consult.
They said () = an answer.
God said unto Jacob () = the perception of natural good from the Divine.
God said unto him () = a perception from the Divine. Explained.
The midwife said unto her () = a perception from the Natural.
Israel said unto Joseph () = a perception from the Divine Spiritual.
To say () = to perceive and think. AC 4846.
(The men of the place) said () = a perception from truths.
She said to them in saying () = an exhortation; (for) to say... here, = vehement communication.
He said unto him () = a revelation from perception; for revelation is internal [perception, and is from perception. AC 5121.
He said unto Joseph () = the perception of the Celestial in the Natural.
Pharaoh said unto Joseph () = the perception of the Celestial of the Spiritual from the Natural. ( = the perception of the Natural from the Celestial of the Spiritual. AC 5308. AC 5315.)
Joseph said unto Pharaoh () = the perception of the Natural from the Celestial of the Spiritual.
Pharaoh said unto his servants () = the perception of the Natural with all things there.
As Joseph had said () = as foreseen by the Celestial of the Spiritual. To say... when predicated of the Lord, = to perceive from Himself, thus to foresee.
Pharaoh said to all Egypt () = an apperception... in both Naturals.
He confirms with himself that they are truths [merely] because others have said so.
Jacob said to his sons () = a perception concerning truths in general.
Joseph said unto them () = a perception concerning that Thing of which his brethren had spoken. AC 5458.
They said a man to his brother () = a perception concerning the cause. Explained.
(One of them) said unto his brethren () = a general perception. Explained.
The man, the lord of the land, said unto us () = an apperception concerning the Celestial of the Spiritual reigning in the Natural. (Compare AC 5591.)

Jacob their father said unto them () = a [perception with them from the good of truth. ( = a perception from the things of the Church. AC 5581.) ( = a perception from spiritual good. AC 5595. AC 5616.)
Reuben said unto his father () = the things which are of faith in the understanding apperceived by the good of truth.
Judah said unto Israel his father () = a perception from the good of the Church concerning these things.
They said, Thy servant our father hath peace () = thence an apperception of the Natural that it is well with the good a quo.
The reason to say = to perceive, is that in Heaven the very thoughts from which is the speech are perceived...
As to say = perception relatively to him who hears and receives, it = to inflow relatively to him who says; for they mutually respond.
They said unto him () = apperception.
Joseph said unto them () = their perception then... The reason it = their perception, is that Joseph says, who = the Internal, through which comes all perception.
Judah said () = a perception given to the good of the Church in the Natural.
Ae said to my lord () = a reciprocal perception.
Thou saidst to thy servants () = a perception given. AC 5814.
Our father said () = an apperception from spiritual good. ( = a perception from spiritual good). AC 5825.
I said () = an apperception...
Joseph said unto his brethren () = that the Celestial Internal gave the faculty of perception to the truths in the Natural. ( = the perception of the new Natural. AC 5882.)
Say ye unto him, Thus saith thy son Joseph () = the perception (of spiritual good) concerning the Celestial Internal.
Pharaoh said unto Joseph () = the perception of the Natural from the Celestial Internal.
He said unto them () = a perception given by the Internal.
They told him, saying () = influx and apperception.
They are ruled by truths when the truth is acknowledged because the Lord has said so in the Word.
Israel said unto Joseph () = the perception of spiritual good from the Celestial Internal. AC 6302.
Joseph said unto his brethren () = the perception of the truths in the Natural from the Celestial Internal.
Pharaoh said unto (Joseph's) brethren () = the perception (of the Natural) concerning the truths of the Church in the Natural.
Pharaoh said unto Joseph, saying () = a perception in the Natural where scientifics are... Joseph = the Internal, whence is the perception in the Natural.
Pharaoh said unto Jacob () = a perception in the Natural where scientifics are, concerning the general truth of the Church.

Joseph said unto the people () = the influx of the Internal into scientific truths... As to say is predicated of the Internal, it = influx; for that which is perceived in the external inflows from the internal.
(One) said unto Joseph () = eminent apperception. Explained.
Jacob said unto Joseph () = the communication of natural truth with the Internal... For that which is perceived by another, is communicated.
Israel said unto Joseph () = elevation to the Internal. Explained.
Joseph said unto his father () = a perceptible influx. Explained.
Thus shall ye say to Joseph () = a perception from the Internal what to do.
The king of Egypt said... () = influx from separated scientifics...
The midwives said... () = apperception concerning these scientific truths...
He said unto his daughters () = thought concerning the holy things of the Church.
Moses said () perception from the law which is from the Divine.
To say, when predicated of Jehovah, = not perception, but omniscience. Explained.
Moses said unto God () = perception from the Divine, and humiliation. AC 6980.
Say unto them () = instruction.
Ye shall say unto him () = influx. Explained.
Jehovah said unto him () = foresight what their quality would be. (For) to say, when predicated of Jehovah, = foresight. AC 6959.
Jehovah said unto Moses () = Providence by the Divine; (for) to say, when predicated of Jehovah, = foresight, and therefore also Providence... AC 6964.
Jehovah said unto him () = Divine influx.
Jehovah said unto Moses () = a perception from the Divine.
Thou shalt say unto Pharaoh () = exhortation. For to say, when done from a Divine command, = exhortation. AC 7090.
I say unto thee () = a command. AC 7234.
Pharaoh said () = contrary thought. Explained. AC 7103.

Pharaoh said () = the will of those who are infesting the truths of the Church... The reason to 8ay = to will, or will, is that it involves the things which follow; for, when anyone wills anything, he says it. As to say involves the things which follow, it = various things; as a command, exhortation, communication, thought; properly, perception. References.
Jehovah said unto Moses () = instruction concerning the law Divine; (for) Jehovah said = instruction from the Divine. AC 7267. AC 7288.

We often read Jehovah said, and Jehovah spake... which repetition = nothing else than something new there beginning, which, however, is to be connected with what precedes. That Jehovah said = what is new of perception. References.

Say to the sons of Israel () = that the law Divine shall give those of the Spiritual Kingdom to apperceive... To say = to apperceive; here, to give to apperceive, because it is said concerning the law Divine that it should say.

Moses said before Jehovah () = thought concerning the law Divine [as it exists] with those who are in falsities... For when he said is said, and by it is signified thought, that which follows is involved.
It was said to me, that... AC 7249. AC 7250.
Thou shalt say unto Aaron () = the influx and communication of the law Divine with doctrine... To say, here, = the like as to speak, namely, both influx and communication.
Jehovah said unto Moses () = Divine instruction; (for) he said, when anything is commanded anew, = instruction, here, Divine instruction, because Jehovah said.
Thou shalt say unto him () = a command; (for) to say, when done by the law Divine... to those in falsities... = a command.
Jehovah said unto Moses () = execution, as is evident from the things which follow.
Jehovah said unto Moses () = new instruction, (because) something new is commanded. AC 7380. AC 7434. AC 7517. AC 7672. AC 7765.
What to say involves in the historicals... is evident from the things which follow it, for it involves them.
Say unto Aaron () = the influx of the internal law into the external law. Explained.
Moses said unto Pharaoh () = an answer. AC 7594. AC 7725. AC 7739.
The magicians said unto Pharaoh () = a perception and communication with those in evils.
Thus saith Jehovah the God of the Hebrews () = a command from the Lord who is the God of the Church. AC 7539. AC 7567. AC 7630. AC 7639.
(Pharaoh) said unto them () = humiliation, as is evident from the things which follow.
(Moses and Aaron) said unto (Pharaoh) () = apperception... because they = truth Divine... and, from the presence of (this) there is apperception.
The servants of Pharaoh said unto him () = an admonition from those who were in fear.
(Pharaoh) said unto (Moses and Aaron) () = an inclination, as is evident from the things which follow... This will, or inclination, is contained in he said unto them.
He said unto them () = mockery, as is evident from the words which Pharaoh says.
Pharaoh said to him () = the wrath of anger then against the truth. For to say involves the things which follow.
Now say in the ears of the people () = information and obedience. AC 7793.
Moses said, Thus said Jehovah () = instruction.

Jehovah said unto Closes and unto Aaron () = information through truth Divine. For to say, when by Jehovah concerning the things to be instituted in the Church, = information; for to say involves the things sequent. AC 8041.
(Moses) said unto (the elders of Israel) () = a perception.
Your sons shall say unto you () = an interior perception of the truth which is of conscience. (Explained.)
Ye shall say () = thought... because this is the answer.
Moses said unto the people () = instruction through truth Divine. For to say, when through truth Divine concerning the things to be observed in the Church, = instruction. References.
God said () = the Divine foresight.
Pharaoh will say... () = the thought of those in damnation...
They said () = a chiding.
They said unto Moses () = the height and desperation of temptation; for the things which follow are involved in they said.
Moses said unto the people () = an elevation from the state of despair through truth Divine.
Thus said Jehovah unto Moses () = an exhortation, (because) it treats of elevation and deliverance from temptation.
The Egyptians said () = the thought of those in falsities from evil. To say, when evil is assailing, = thought.
Jehovah said unto Moses () = influx, (because) it treats of the exercise of the dominion of power through Divine truth.
They said in saying () = thus from influx, (because) it treats of the Glorification of the Lord by a song.
The enemy said () = the thought of those in evils and derivative falsities before the Lord's advent.
And He said () = instruction, (because) by Jehovah concerning a truth of order as to temptations.
The Spirits of Jupiter... consider what they say...
The sons of Israel said unto them () = thought from anxiety.
Jehovah said unto Moses () = consolation from the Lord.
Moses and Aaron said unto all the sons of Israel () = information by truth Divine. AC 8430. AC 8463.
Moses said unto Aaron () = the influx of the truth Divine which proceeds immediately from the Lord through that which proceeds mediately. AC 8529.
Say unto all the congregation... () = instruction. Explained. AC 8492.
They said a man unto his brother () = amazement. Explained.
Moses said unto them () = exhortation. (Explained.)
Jehovah said unto Moses () = the appearance of the Divine obscured with them. Explained.

Moses said to them () = an answer through influx into the thought. To say, when from truth Divine... = an answer; and, as all answer from the Divine is effected through influx, and that into the thought, the above is signified.
Jehovah said unto Moses () = aid. Explained. ( = instruction. AC 8619. AC 8929. AC 9414. AC 10537.)
Moses said unto Joshua () = Divine influx into truth combating.
(Jethro) said unto Moses () = influx and the consequent perception. Explained. ( = foresight. AC 8697.)
Moses said to his father-in-law () = what is reciprocal which is in the reply. Explained.
To say, and to announce () = Salvation. Explained.

Jehovah said unto Moses () = a revelation concerning the preparation; (for) to say, when said by Jehovah, = revelation from the Divine. ( = an exhortation by the Divine. AC 8829.) ( = an admonition. AC 8839.)
Moses said unto Jehovah () = the thought of truth from the Divine.

For that which is said first must be kept in the memory in the things which follow, and be regarded as what is universal therein. The things which have been said by the Lord are such; namely, that the things said first must reign in those which follow, and involve them...
They said unto Moses () = a complaint.
Moses said unto the people () = information. Explained. ( = instruction. AC 10728.)
Those of the Spiritual Church... do not know from any internal perception that what the Church says is true, but solely from the fact that the Church says so they confirm it...
If in saying the servant shall say () = thought then from the implanted truth.
All that Jehovah has said unto them () = all things which are of life, of worship, and of the civil state.
And He said unto Moses () = that which concerns the Word in general. Explained.
Jehovah said unto Moses () = illustration and perception again by the Lord through the Word. To say, when predicated of Jehovah, = illustration and perception. References. AC 10354.
(The people) said unto Aaron () = exhortation. AC 10473. AC 10486.
Aaron said () = what was perceived. (Explained.)
Moses said unto Jehovah () = indignation that the Divine... was not with them.

Jehovah said unto Moses () = what is concluded concerning the Israelitish nation... For He said involves the things which follow, because these are the things which He said, or which are said. ( = information. AC 10682.)
(These Spirits) recite some sayings from the sense of the letter, and note the Society with which communication is effected.
It has been told me from Heaven...
To say () = confession.
They could not say One God.
None of the clergy could say Divine Human...
To fly in the midst of Heaven, and say () = to perceive and understand; and, when predicated of the Lord, to look out for and provide; here, to instruct and preach.
Said, being used twice, () = that it may be known with certainty.
He said to me () = that it is Divine truth, because the Lord said the third time He said to me... and what the Lord says the third time is what must be believed because it is the Divine Truth...

They then said with a half utterance, Yes, yes; we apprehend. But the Angel said, Turn yourselves a little away from me, and say in like manner. They did so, and said with a full utterance, It is not so.
Those from the east replied. We will speak; but as man does not take anything from himself... we will speak from the Lord, and still from ourselves, as if from ourselves...
The penalty of those who do not say what they think...
They were informed that they must by no means say differently from what they think, except in the last necessity.
Thou sayest () = what is believed by them.
To say, in the spiritual sense, = to think, because that which is said comes forth from the thought, and thought is spiritual... and saying is natural. Hence to say has many significations.
Saying () = confession: for a confession follows.
To answer and say, () when done by the elders, by whom is signified Heaven where the Lord is, = influx and perception...
He said to me () = information.
Saying with a great voice () = a manifestation.
He said to me () = a Divine command (because), by an Angel, by whom is represented the Lord as to the Word; for what the Lord says is a command. AE 628.
To say () = boasting.
The sayings of Scripture by which Truths are confirmed, ascend into Heaven: they are like the smoke from incense.
